items.followUp: State the main conclusions drawn from Rutherford’s alpha-particle scattering experiment.

rubric.why: Most alpha particles passed through the foil without deflection.
rubric.description: States that most alpha particles passed straight through the foil.

rubric.why: A small number of alpha particles changed direction, and a very few were reflected backwards.
rubric.description: States that some alpha particles were deflected and very few bounced back.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either deflection or backward scattering.

modelAnswer: Most alpha particles passed straight through the gold foil without any deflection.
Some alpha particles were deflected, while a very few bounced back.

items.followUp: Name one use of uranium-235 in a nuclear reactor.

rubric.description: Identifies nuclear fission as the process involving U-235.

rubric.why: Uranium-235 is used as fuel in nuclear reactors and can also be used in atomic weapons.
rubric.description: States a use of U-235, such as nuclear-reactor fuel or an atomic bomb.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any correct use.

modelAnswer: Uranium-235 is used as a fuel in nuclear reactors, where it undergoes nuclear fission to release energy.
It is also used in the manufacture of atomic bombs.

items.followUp: Define ionization energy and electron affinity.

rubric.why: Electron affinity concerns the energy change when an isolated gaseous atom accepts an electron.
rubric.description: Defines electron affinity in terms of a gaseous atom accepting an electron and the associated energy change.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the essential idea of electron acceptance and energy change.

rubric.why: Electronegativity describes the attraction exerted by an atom on shared electrons in a chemical bond.
rubric.description: Defines electronegativity as an atom’s tendency to attract shared electrons in a bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the attraction of shared/bonding electrons.

modelAnswer: Electron affinity is the energy change when an isolated gaseous atom accepts an electron to form a negative ion.
Electronegativity is the ability of an atom in a molecule to attract the shared pair of electrons towards itself.

items.followUp: State the two main ideas of Newlands’ law of octaves.

rubric.why: A Dobereiner triad consists of three elements with similar chemical properties.
rubric.description: States that a triad contains three elements with similar properties.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the three-element grouping and similarity.

rubric.why: The atomic mass of the middle element is approximately the arithmetic mean of the other two.
rubric.description: States the approximate atomic-mass relationship for the middle element.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the average-mass relationship.

modelAnswer: Dobereiner arranged some elements with similar chemical properties in groups of three, called triads.
In a triad, the atomic mass of the middle element was approximately the average of the atomic masses of the other two elements.

items.followUp: How many electrons are present in the outer shell of an atom following the octet rule?

rubric.why: A duplet is a stable arrangement with two electrons in the outermost shell.
rubric.description: Defines the duplet rule as stability with two outer-shell electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the two-electron stable arrangement.

rubric.why: An octet is a stable arrangement with eight electrons in the outermost shell.
rubric.description: Defines the octet rule as stability with eight outer-shell electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the eight-electron stable arrangement.

modelAnswer: The duplet rule states that an atom is stable when its outermost shell contains two electrons.
The octet rule states that an atom is stable when its outermost shell contains eight electrons.

rubric.why: The term distinguishes forces between molecules from forces within a molecule.
rubric.description: Identifies that these forces act between separate molecules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the between-molecules relationship.

rubric.why: Intermolecular forces are forces of attraction between molecules.
rubric.description: Identifies the forces as attractive forces.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they are attractive.

modelAnswer: Intermolecular forces are forces of attraction between molecules.
They act between separate molecules, rather than holding the atoms within a molecule together.

items.followUp: Why does water have its maximum density at 4°C?

rubric.why: Ice has a lower density than liquid water.
rubric.description: States that ice is less dense than liquid water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the density comparison.

rubric.why: Hydrogen bonding forms an open structure in ice, increasing its volume and lowering its density.
rubric.description: Explains the lower density using the open structure or increased volume of ice.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the structural reason.

modelAnswer: Ice floats on water because it is less dense than liquid water.
Hydrogen bonds form an open structure in ice, so the same mass occupies a greater volume.

items.followUp: Define diffusion and give one example of diffusion in a liquid.

rubric.why: Diffusion is the spreading or movement of gas particles from a region of higher concentration to one of lower concentration.
rubric.description: Defines diffusion as the spreading/movement of gas particles, ideally from higher to lower concentration.

rubric.why: A suitable example illustrates gas particles spreading, such as perfume smell spreading through a room.
rubric.description: Gives a valid example of gas diffusion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example.

modelAnswer: Diffusion of a gas is the spreading of its particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration.
For example, the smell of perfume spreads through a room by diffusion.
